analysis.title: The Wolfe Power Trip: FCF yields approach recent history, AI trade correlations
key_insights: Wolfe lowers its utilities sentiment meter by one notch to 3. The IPPs were hit hard as the AI trade came under pressure: first the CRWV selloff, then SPCX earnings gave some relief, then more pressure after META earnings.

Midterm elections are approaching and political rhetoric around data centers remains tricky. Wolfe says little changed fundamentally for the stocks, and it saw improvement after CEG's GOOGL/AMZN deals and FERC rejecting IRAS.

Wolfe has a relative preference for the PJM names, CEG first and then TLN, heading into Q3 earnings. Commodities have been stronger and regulatory fears have eased (IRAS, state commentary on the future of the capacity market).

Guidance expectations: softer 2027 guidance for NRG, VST still waiting on Cogentrix to close and may not give a 2028 outlook, TLN's outlook through 2029 mostly in line, CEG's guide refresh to come on Q4.
IPP two-year forward EV/EBITDA is 8.0x as of 10/23/26 against a 15-year average of 7.8x. It briefly hit the average earlier this summer, bounced, then mostly retraced.

IPP average FCF yield is about 11% today against a 9% average since the start of the AI trade (early 2024) and a 12% average since CEG began trading in February 2022. The 10-year average is 16.0%. This is near the highest FCF yield since the AI boom began.

By name: TLN's FCF yield is above its history even including TLN 1.0. NRG is slightly above its long-run average. CEG is in line with its 5-year average. VST is the only one notably below its average.

Wolfe argues the IPPs have stronger businesses than in the past: rising long-term contracted cash flows, lower leverage and demand growth. It calls it a misconception that IPPs hit peak earnings in 2027-2028, citing data center deal ramps, commodity curves not in backwardation, and excess FCF going to buybacks.

2027 FCF yields do not capture recent contracts in full. CEG's FCF excludes the AMZN/GOOGL nuclear deals (3.2 GW) and only part of the Crane restart. TLN's includes only the first 360 MW of the Susquehanna contract, which ramps to 1,920 MW. VST's includes half of the 2.2 GW META nuclear PPA and essentially none of the 1.2 GW AMZN Comanche Peak PPA.

IPPs were about 80% correlated with Wolfe's equal-weighted AI basket in 2025. They decoupled in 2026 on the White House/PJM Statement of Principles and then recoupled during the latest drawdown. Wolfe sees the businesses as increasingly defensive although the stocks do not trade defensively.

FERC ruled on PJM's RBP on 9/29, partially accepting it. PJM is expected to file a 205 with revisions by 10/29, and FERC then has 60 days. PJM targets a central procurement starting 3/1/27, with final results posted 5/3/27.
FERC largely denied PJM's IRAS proposal on 10/9, accepting only the large load registry. The compliance filing is due 11/8.

PJM's 2028/2029 capacity auction cleared at the cap of $325/MW-day, 6.8 GW short of the reliability requirement. It would have priced at $555/MW-day uncapped. The 2029/2030 auction runs in December 2026 with results posted 12/22 and is the last with the collar.
VST's $4.0B Cogentrix acquisition (5.5 GW) has FERC approval from 8/5 and state approvals. DoJ approval is the remaining step and close is expected late 2026.
ERCOT Batch Zero eligibility report is due 12/10 ahead of the PUCT meeting on 12/17. ERCOT sees 66 GW of base load in Batch Zero.

market_movers.rationale: Wolfe's relative preference among PJM names heading into Q3. FCF yield is in line with its 5-year average, and recent AMZN/GOOGL deals are not in the 2027 FCF.
Second preference after CEG. FCF yield is above history, and the Susquehanna contract is only partly captured in estimates.
Cheapest of the group on FCF yield, but Wolfe expects softer 2027 guidance.
FCF yield is the only one notably below its own history. Cogentrix has not closed and a 2028 outlook may not be given.

sector_views.rationale: Wolfe sees valuation near historical averages on FCF yield, stronger contracted cash flows and lower leverage, with a relative preference for PJM names (CEG, then TLN).

earnings_insights: Wolfe expects softer 2027 guidance from NRG in Q3 earnings. VST may not give a 2028 outlook. TLN's outlook through 2029 should be mostly in line. CEG's guide refresh comes with Q4.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Cleared at the cap, 6.8 GW short of the reliability requirement, and would have been $555/MW-day uncapped.
Market gas prices are 10.6% below Wolfe's assumption for 2026.
Market 2027 PJM West power is above Wolfe's assumption.

risk_factors: AI trade drawdown (CRWV, META earnings) continues to pressure IPPs.
Political rhetoric around data centers ahead of the midterm elections.
Regulatory risk in PJM: RBP revisions, capacity market reform and governance, FERC rulings.
ERCOT Batch Zero timing and data center verification delays.

vol_and_positioning: IPPs recoupled with the AI trade during the latest drawdown after decoupling earlier in 2026.
Funds seemed to flow back into the IPPs from higher-beta AI names before the latest downturn.

tension_points.bull_case: FCF yields near 11% are close to averages since CEG began trading (12%), contracted cash flows are rising, leverage is lower, and 2027 estimates do not capture recent nuclear deals in full.
tension_points.bear_case: IPPs recoupled with the AI basket in the latest drawdown, political rhetoric around data centers ahead of the midterms is tricky, and yields remain well below the 16.0% 10-year average.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further AI trade pressure and regulatory setbacks in PJM, such as FERC action on the RBP revisions, would pressure the group.
